findings.title: Google refresh stores Zod safeParse envelope instead of token data
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but this line assigns that entire object to `key` and saves it as `credential.key`. The Google credential schema expects the token object itself (access_token, refresh_token, expiry_date). After one successful refresh, the stored credential no longer parses, breaking Google Calendar authentication.

findings.title: Broken minimum token schema and placeholder refresh_token corrupt credentials
findings.body: The `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, which do not create a Zod index signature; they only create literal properties. Since Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, sync-mode parsing removes refresh tokens, expiry fields, and provider-specific fields such as instance_url. The function then inserts the literal string "refresh_token" when `refresh_token` is missing. Saving this result can overwrite real refresh tokens or required metadata, leaving credentials unusable.

findings.title: Salesforce credential refresh uses undefined prisma import
findings.body: This file calls `prisma.credential.update` but does not import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. This will fail type checking and cause a runtime ReferenceError when Salesforce token refresh is attempted.

findings.title: Sync-mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response for callers expecting different types
findings.body: When credential sharing is enabled, this function bypasses the provider refresh function and returns the raw `fetch` Response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Callers were not updated to a common contract: Google expects a response with `.data`, HubSpot expects a parsed token object, and ZohoCRM/Bigin expect an Axios response with `.data`. In those integrations the returned Response lacks the expected properties, causing undefined access and failed token refreshes.

findings.title: Bigin token refresh sends credential ID as calcomUserId
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects a Cal.com user ID, but this call passes `credentialId`, the credential primary key. The external sync endpoint will receive `calcomUserId` equal to a credential ID, not the user's ID, so it cannot identify the correct user token to return.

findings.title: Salesforce client is created with stale access token after refresh
findings.body: After fetching a new access token and updating the credential, the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still constructed with `credentialKey.access_token`, the old access token. The newly fetched `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` is not used, so API calls may continue to use an expired token.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh is not synced but still uses the destructive minimum schema
findings.body: Salesforce token refresh does not call `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it does not use the configured external sync endpoint. However it does call `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which switches to the minimal sync schema when credential sharing is enabled. That minimal schema strips required Salesforce fields such as `instance_url` before the credential is saved, corrupting Salesforce credentials.

findings.title: Zoho CRM token validity check is inverted
findings.body: `isTokenValid` returns true when `expiryDate < Date.now()`, i.e. when the token is expired. `getToken` then resolves without refreshing when `isTokenValid` is true and refreshes when it is false. This causes expired Zoho CRM tokens to be used and valid tokens to be refreshed unnecessarily.

findings.title: Credential webhook does not reset invalid flag on update
findings.body: When updating an existing credential, the handler only updates `key`. If the credential was previously marked `invalid`, it remains invalid even after new synced keys are written. The update should also set `invalid: false` when accepting new credentials.

findings.title: Credential webhook find-then-update/create can duplicate credentials
findings.body: The handler searches for an existing credential and then creates or updates it without a transaction or unique constraint. Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both miss the existing record and create duplicates. If duplicates already exist, `findFirst` updates an arbitrary one.

findings.title: Webhook handler accepts all HTTP methods
findings.body: The handler does not check `req.method`, so any HTTP method can reach the credential creation/update logic if the secret header is supplied. It should only accept POST and reject other methods with 405.

findings.title: Unhandled Zod, decryption, and JSON parse errors return 500
findings.body: Zod parsing of the request body, symmetric decryption, and `JSON.parse` of the decrypted payload can throw. There is no try/catch to convert invalid payloads into a 400 response, so malformed webhook requests result in 500 errors.

findings.title: Credential sync endpoint is called without authentication or response validation
findings.body: The outbound sync request sends `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` without any authentication, signature, or shared secret, and it does not validate `response.ok` before returning. If the endpoint is reachable, callers may accept forged or malformed token responses, and failures are not handled explicitly.

findings.title: Team credential creation lacks admin check
findings.body: When OAuth state includes `teamId`, the code only verifies that the user is an accepted team member before creating a team credential. It does not check that the user has admin access to the team. Because OAuth state is client-supplied JSON, a non-admin team member can craft a state with a team id and create team app credentials.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh checks statusText instead of response.ok
findings.body: Using `response.statusText !== "OK"` to detect OAuth failure is unreliable; HTTP/2 and some fetch implementations return an empty statusText even for successful responses. This can cause successful token refreshes to throw. Use `response.ok` or the HTTP status code instead.

findings.title: No tests for credential sync webhook and token refresh changes
findings.body: This PR adds a secret-authenticated credential ingestion endpoint and changes token refresh behavior across many providers, but no tests are included. Tests are needed for webhook authentication/validation, idempotent credential create/update, and refresh behavior with credential sync enabled and disabled.
